Festive Spiced Nuts

Served at: Fourth Sunday of Advent

Yields about 4 cups (450 g)Prep 15 minCook 30-35 min

These aromatic, crunchy spiced nuts are a perfect treat for the Fourth Sunday of Advent, offering warmth and comfort as Christmas approaches. They make a wonderful snack for holiday gatherings, a thoughtful homemade gift, or a cozy accompaniment to an evening of carols and reflection.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (450 g) mixed nuts (such as pecans, walnuts, almonds, cashews)
  • 1 large egg white
  • 1 tablespoon (15 mL) water
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar
  • 2 tablespoons (25 g) light brown sugar, packed
  • 1 teaspoon (2 g) ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon (1 g) ground nutmeg
  • 1/2 teaspoon (1 g) ground ginger
  • 1/4 teaspoon (0.5 g) ground cloves
  • 1/4 teaspoon (0.5 g) ground allspice
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 g) fine sea salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon (0.5 g) cayenne pepper (optional, for a subtle kick)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat.
  2. In a large bowl, whisk together the egg white and water until frothy.
  3. Add the mixed nuts to the egg white mixture and toss well to ensure all nuts are evenly coated.
  4. In a small bowl, combine the granulated sugar, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, cloves, allspice, salt, and cayenne pepper (if using). Stir until thoroughly mixed.
  5. Sprinkle the spice mixture over the egg white-coated nuts. Toss vigorously until all the nuts are completely and evenly coated with the spice mixture.
  6. Spread the seasoned nuts in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
  7. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring the nuts every 10-15 minutes to ensure even roasting and prevent burning. The nuts should be fragrant and feel dry to the touch.
  8. Remove the baking sheet from the oven and let the nuts cool completely on the baking sheet. They will become crispier as they cool.
  9. Once cooled, break apart any clusters and store the spiced nuts in an airtight container at room temperature.

Tips

  • For a different flavor profile, try adding a pinch of cardamom or a teaspoon of orange zest to the spice mixture.
  • Ensure the nuts are completely cool before storing; otherwise, condensation can make them soft.
  • These nuts can be stored in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks, making them perfect for preparing ahead of holiday festivities.
